_comment: Benchmarks the nightly job must report (T-1801), checked by tools/benchmark/compare_benchmarks.py --required. Keys are className.testName; each listed metric prefix must match at least one reported metric. A benchmark that is intentionally not run by the job goes under optional with its reason. A result that is neither required nor optional fails the gate, so a renamed test cannot slip through. The listed metrics are the ones a GitHub-hosted emulator reports: it has no SurfaceFlinger frame timeline, so FrameTimingMetric yields frameCount alone and the jank metrics frameDurationCpuMs and frameOverrunMs of plan §9 need a physical device (ADR-0018 addendum).

optional.ir.taqvim.benchmark.BaselineProfileGener: Excluded from the nightly job (notClass); run on demand by :app:generateBaselineProfile.

optional.ir.taqvim.benchmark.micro.GlanceWidgetBe: Run, but neither required nor a control yet: a benchmark cannot be either before a baseline exists for it, and every control must be required (the gate's own test says so, because a control that is not required could vanish unnoticed). The hosted run that first reported this one had its controls drift by 60 %, so its numbers are no reference. Once a healthy hosted run records a baseline, move it to required and to control, where it belongs: it times GlanceAppWidget.compose with nothing to compose, which no app change can move. On the OnePlus 15 on 2026-10-10 that was 406.07 ms, and every real widget came out 1.45-10.57 ms above it.

control._comment: Runner-health control (T-1801). These microbenchmarks time fixed synthetic drawing and mask computation in process, with no UI, no frame timeline and no dataset, so a change to the app's screens or data cannot move them. When they move far, the machine moved: both degraded nightly runs blew them up while the code that draws them was byte-identical to the baseline commit (run 35953669737 sunArcBitmap +348.8 %, progressRingBitmap +241.3 %; run 36040359691 progressRingBitmap +258.4 %, moonBitmap +75.6 %). A control outside its band makes the whole comparison inconclusive rather than failed, because timings from that machine cannot be trusted. Editing the code one of these benchmarks draws means its baseline must be re-recorded, as for any benchmark. GlanceWidgetBenchmark.emptyBaseline belongs here too and is not listed yet only because it has no baseline: it composes a widget that draws nothing, so it times GlanceAppWidget.compose itself, and a widget's own composition cost is its figure minus that one. That subtraction is not an assumption; it was measured on the OnePlus 15 on 2026-10-10, where the empty widget cost 406.07 ms and the real widgets came out 1.45-10.57 ms above it.
